test.name: Locality guide for California, 1850s — Gold Rush migration records
test.description: Verifies that the skill recognizes California’s statehood in 1850 and highlights records created during the Gold Rush era. Ensures guidance includes mining claims, land deeds, census schedules, and local court records, while noting challenges such as transient populations and incomplete documentation.

input.delegation: I'm researching ancestors in California during the 1850s Gold Rush. What records or repositories would help trace people who migrated there for mining or settlement?

judge_context: Recognize California became a state in 1850 and mention Gold Rush-specific records (mining claims, land deeds, and census schedules). Repositories count when a tool result names them (e.g. the California State Library, the Bancroft Library at UC Berkeley, the National Archives at San Bruno, county recorders' offices); a guide that reports that no tool confirmed a state archives, courthouse holding or church archive for the period is correct, not incomplete. Mission-era and Spanish/Mexican records may appear only flagged as pre-period background; presenting them as a source or substitute for 1850s research is an error. Newspapers may be named as a record class, and the external_links_search Newspapers.com link is a grounded generic link; no tool here returns a California newspaper title, so reporting that none was confirmed is a correct gap report, not an omission, while naming specific titles or coverage would be ungrounded. Dock this: external_links_search returns only each link's URL and link text, so assigning a repository an access level (Free, Subscription, paid) the link text does not state is ungrounded; so is presenting a modern database as if it existed in the 1850s.

volume_search returns a total of 14 results, with more available via a next-page token, including an 88%-indexed, full-text-searchable 1850-1852 state census volume (imageGroupNumber 006601001, 522 images) alongside two large browse-only volumes with 0% indexing (mining claim registers, port arrival registers). Citing the 88% figure, the image count, and the imageGroupNumber is a grounded, correct read of the tool response, not a fabrication — do not penalize Correctness for it. The skill should note that more digitized volumes exist beyond the ones it details, rather than implying the result set returned is exhaustive.

No tool here states when California's statewide vital registration began (the wiki_read fetches return only generic content), so a guide that says it could not confirm that date and relies on the 1850 start of the county birth and marriage collections is making a correct gap report, not a vague one. Dock this: giving a year statewide registration began is ungrounded, since no tool here gives one.
